title: Support For Home-Based Businesses During COVID-19 Circuit Breaker Period
what_it_is: Support For Home-Based Businesses During COVID-19 Circuit Breaker Period

sections.label: Home-based businesses delivery ban
sections.summary: Some home-based businesses observed circuit breaker measures, but the ban on all deliveries cut off their income.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I know of individuals doing HBBs who steadfastly observed the CB measures as they went about delivering their orders, or when they engaged third-party delivery companies to deliver their orders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, the recent move to ban all deliveries by HBBs has cut off this income stream, and for some, the only source of income, for their families.

sections.label: Cancelled orders and discarded ingredients
sections.summary: Many home-based businesses had to cancel or hold orders, make refunds, and discard purchased raw ingredients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For many of the HBBs, orders have had to be cancelled or put on hold, refunds have had to be made, and to some extent, raw ingredients already purchased have had to be discarded.

sections.label: Home businesses as only income
sections.summary: For some, home baking, cooking or selling crafts is their only income for food and daily expenses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Home baking or cooking, or selling their crafts or other items from home is their only source of income, without which, they will be unable to put food on the table or pay for daily expenses.

sections.label: Violet Frost cake seller
sections.summary: She sells frosted cakes from home through Violet Frost to earn income and care for her son with spina bifida.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: She sells beautiful cakes with frosting through Violet Frost.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: She bakes from home so that she is able to earn an income to support her children and at the same time be at home to take care of her 10-year-old son who has spina bifida.

sections.label: Ms Tan selling baked goods
sections.summary: Ms Tan has sold cakes, brownies and cookies full-time since graduating from university last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Ms Tan has been selling cakes, brownies and cookies full-time since graduating from University last year.

sections.label: Home-based businesses resume operations
sections.summary: Home-based businesses will be allowed to resume operations from 12 May with some restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our HBB owners, they embody our nation's DNA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that from 12 May, HBBs will be allowed to resume operations, with some restrictions.

sections.label: Third-party delivery for HBBs
sections.summary: Authorities will allow HBBs to engage third-party delivery companies, as F&B establishments already do for food and drinks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One, I understand the authorities will allow HBBs to engage the services of third-party delivery companies, much like how Food and Beverage (F&B) establishments are already doing to deliver their food and drinks.

sections.label: F&B central kitchens for HBBs
sections.summary: Some F&B establishments are offering the use of their central kitchens to HBBs who may be keen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Three, some F&B establishments are offering the use of their central kitchens to HBBs who may be keen to do so.

sections.label: Co-funding central kitchen costs
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider co-funding central kitchen running costs for a defined period to help businesses recover.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider co-funding the cost of running these central kitchens for a defined period of time to allow the retail and home-based businesses involved some time to get back on their feet?

sections.label: Equal opportunity and consistent restrictions
sections.summary: HBBs ask for equal opportunity to continue business like other retail establishments while observing restrictions, plus clarity and consistency in applying restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: All they ask, is for an equal opportunity to continue their business like other retail establishments whilst still observing restricted measures in place; as well as clarity and consistency in applying any restrictions that are in place.

sections.label: Empathy, resilience and inclusive solutions
sections.summary: HBBs ask for empathy, understanding and leadership in inclusive solutions, and the speaker hopes to highlight their challenges, resilience and dignity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And all they are asking for is some empathy and understanding of their situation, and leadership in arriving at inclusive solutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that in doing this Adjournment Motion, I am able to, in some small measure, highlight the challenges faced by, and the resilience and dignity of, our HBBs in taking charge of their lives and livelihoods, without expecting handouts or financial help from others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Their resilience and dignity to support themselves and their families ought to be celebrated, and they should not be admonished when they give feedback or ask for a level playing field to carry on their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More importantly, going forward, what are the lessons we can learn from this current episode that will help us manage, navigate and lead in future crises, where we listen and understand first, not have knee-jerk reactions, and co-create solutions in an inclusive manner?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to thank President Halimah Yacob and Minister Lawrence Wong for showing empathy and understanding of the hardship and challenges that HBBs face.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, by Barack Obama, and I quote, "I believe a stronger sense of empathy would tilt the balance of our current politics in favour of those people who are struggling in this society.

sections.label: HBB access to SIRS
sections.summary: Asks for confirmation that Home-Business Owners in financial distress can apply for SIRS, and whether SIRS applies to all HBB owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As the Temporary Relief Fund has ended, can I have a confirmation that Home-Business Owners can apply for the Self-Employed Relief Scheme or SIRS if they are in financial distress?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, is SIRS applicable to all HBB owners as they could be full-time or seasonal in carrying out their business?

sections.label: Home-Based Business relief advice
sections.summary: HBB owners are advised to file for relief under the COVID-19 Temporary Measures Bill, but most lack a Scheduled Contract and cannot avail themselves of the reliefs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The advice given to these Home-Based Business (HBB) owners is to file for relief under COVID-19 Temporary Measures Bill for Ministry of Law to decide on the final settlement if the HBBs' agreements can be classified as a "Scheduled Contract".

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The reality is that most HBB do not have "Scheduled Contract" and will not be able to avail themselves of the reliefs under the Act.

sections.label: Supporting wages and welfare
sections.summary: Everyone is urged to support efforts to boost wages and improve welfare, even at higher cost, through the Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And to all of us, regardless whether you are a service buyer, service provider or end consumer, let us do the right thing and support efforts to boost their wages and improve their welfare, even if it means at a higher cost to us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have the means through our Progressive Wage Model to make this happen.

sections.label: Circuit breaker imposed
sections.summary: On 7 April, the circuit breaker was imposed to decisively curb the spread of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: On 7 April, we imposed the circuit breaker to decisively curb the spread of COVID-19.

sections.label: Essential services tightened
sections.summary: From 21 April, essential services were tightened, barbers, laundromats and dessert stores suspended, and only online-only HBBs allowed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The list of essential services was further tightened from 21 April as the infection rate had not reduced sufficiently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Barbers, laundromats as well as desserts, confectionaries and cake stores suspended their operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We also clarified that only HBBs that operated solely online were allowed, as these do not involve collection and delivery of goods.

sections.label: Community cases halved
sections.summary: The average daily number of new community cases halved from 25 the week before to 12 last week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The average daily number of new cases in the community has halved, from 25 in the week before to 12 last week.

sections.label: Home-based businesses resume operations
sections.summary: The Government allowed home-based businesses to resume from 12 May, with DPPMS advising owners and M3 lawyers offering free legal advice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As we have already seen some results from the tighter measures to break the chain of transmission, the Government has allowed home-based businesses to resume operations from 12 May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DPPMS) is engaging and advising the business owners to tap on the various Government schemes and is also working with lawyers from M3 to offer free legal advice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In its effort to help HBBs from the Malay/Muslim community, DPPMS is exploring ways to help this group for the long run.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: (In English): Let me conclude by assuring Dr Intan, Mr Zainal and the House and the Government stands ready to support workers and businesses have been hit by COVID-19.
